student_answer: Artificial Intelligence refers to the simulation of human intelligence in machines. It allows software to process information, adapt to new inputs, solve problems, and execute tasks like language understanding, pattern detection, and automated decision-making without continuous human intervention.
AI simply means storing a very large amount of information in a computer database.

AI enables machines to carry out tasks that normally need human-like intelligence. AI systems can reason and support decision making. AI can understand language and recognize patterns in text, images, or other data. Applications include chatbots, recommendation systems, image recognition, and automated evaluation.

Machine Learning is a subset of AI that focuses on building algorithms that learn from data. Rather than relying on hardcoded instructions, ML algorithms analyze dataset patterns to make data-driven predictions, continuously improving their accuracy as more data becomes available.
Machine learning is a database technique that only stores and retrieves records faster.

ML is an AI approach that lets software learn patterns from examples. Those learned patterns are used to make predictions or decisions on new inputs. Training examples are used to adjust the model so its performance can improve. Common ML tasks include classification, regression, and prediction.

Natural Language Processing is a discipline within AI that bridges the gap between human communication and computational understanding. It enables systems to analyze, parse, and derive meaning from human text or speech, enabling applications like language translation, sentiment evaluation, and text similarity scoring.
NLP is a networking protocol used to transfer files between computers.

NLP combines AI techniques with language processing so machines can interpret text or speech. NLP can perform text classification and sentiment analysis. Semantic representations can be used to measure text similarity and meaning. In automated grading, NLP can compare a student's response with a reference answer.

Cloud computing involves accessing on-demand computing resources—such as server power, data storage, and software applications—via the internet. It eliminates the need for local hardware infrastructure, offering flexible scaling, remote access, and lower maintenance costs for organizations.
Cloud computing is only a weather forecasting technique that predicts rainfall using computers.

Cloud computing delivers computing resources and services over the internet. Services can include storage, databases, servers, networking, and software. Resources can be scaled up or down according to demand. It means using online computing resources instead of keeping everything on one local computer.

A Database Management System (DBMS) is essential for structured data organization, storage, and retrieval. It ensures high data integrity, handles concurrent user access, enforces security protocols, and prevents data duplication across applications like enterprise platforms, financial institutions, and academic databases.
A DBMS is mainly a graphics program used to design images and animations.

A DBMS provides a structured way to manage and access large collections of data. A DBMS helps maintain data accuracy, integrity, and consistency. It can support many users and applications while reducing unnecessary duplication of data. DBMSs are important in banking, hospitals, education systems, and e-commerce applications.
